title: Hardcoded Buffer Pool Capacities
pattern: Hardcoding fixed buffer block sizes, page layouts, or disk sector segments deep within database or storage engines.
why_bad: Forces excessive logical-to-physical I/O inflating if the underlying storage hardware record size differs (e.g. SSD page sizes are larger). It degrades system bandwidth and induces severe cache thrashing.
detection: The existence of unaligned, hardcoded buffer or page constant variables in low-level I/O engines.
fix: Determine actual filesystem record and sector layouts dynamically at database initialization, adjusting internal page pools to align perfectly.
source: Alex Petrov - *Database Internals_ A Deep Dive Into How Distributed Data Systems Work* (2019, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 11.
